chapter: Piano players, Hot Springs and Chicago
title: Gambling trips to Hot Springs and a stay in Chicago
summary: He went to Hot Springs twice and stayed 60 days in Chicago, returning home to his lottery work paying good money.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah. When your hair has turned silver. That's right. When your hair has turned silver. What were you doing in Hot Springs? You were taking the leg. Well, I had my money. I was making my money so much. Yeah. And you just went up there to take your money? That's right. I went up there twice.

They have plenty of support up there? Well, I could have got a job playing in a nightclub up there. I went and I touched that pen and said, you say, how long are you going to be here, Fred? I said, well, I'm just here for 21 days. I'm going back home. He said, why don't you stay here? You have a job playing at camp if you want. I said, I'm going back to my lottery. I was making an old 250 a week, you know? It was good money 20 years ago. 25, 30 years ago, you know? Did you ever go out to Chicago? Yeah, I stayed in Chicago 60 days. 60 days? 60 days, yeah. I left. See, Campbell the Forest. It started snowing that day and I left. I borrowed money. I spent all my little change I had and I borrowed money to come home.
What year was it? 1922. That's a good one, isn't it?
